## Trial `scheduled-maintenance-rhel9__ukyV2e6`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor correctly scheduled /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance to run daily at 02:15 via root's crontab, ensured crond is enabled/active so the schedule executes, and demonstrated log retention in /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log via a byte-identical manual run of the cron command line. All of this, plus crond/crontab/log state, was independently re-confirmed intact after a full node restart with a directly observed boot-identity change, satisfying the restart-evidence protocol. The delivered script itself contains a pre-existing defect (an embedded literal 'SCRIPT' heredoc terminator causing a 'command not found' line in output each run), but this originates from the prepare-stage script content, not executor action, and does not affect satisfaction of the scheduling/retention contract.

|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

### Comments and limitations

- The actual 02:15 cron-triggered execution was not observed live since that time had not yet occurred; retention was verified via a manual run of the identical command line instead.
- The prepared /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance script contains an internal defect (a stray 'SCRIPT' token producing a 'command not found' error each run); this is preexisting script content, not an executor-introduced issue, but it means the retained log will always include this extra error line.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.950); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.850; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
